title: On Scaling Neuronal Network Simulations Using Distributed Computing
problem: Scaling neuronal network simulations across distributed computing infrastructure while managing network latency and GPU memory constraints. Determining optimal cell distribution strategies for parallel execution in CoreNEURON across multiple geographically distributed sites.
motivation: Large-scale neuronal network simulations enable neuroscience research at biologically realistic scales exceeding conventional single-site system capabilities.
method: The paper characterizes FABRIC infrastructure's computational capabilities emphasizing GPU availability, evaluates cell distribution strategies in CoreNEURON for parallel execution across sites, and applies k-cut graph partitioning algorithms to optimize multi-site performance. Scalability experiments measure network size limits, latency impacts, and GPU memory utilization.
key_novelty: Demonstrating FABRIC distributed infrastructure can effectively scale neuronal network simulations to 25,000 cells using graph partitioning optimization strategies.
contributions: Characterization of FABRIC infrastructure's suitability for neuroscience simulations with GPU performance analysis across 40 sites
Analysis showing cell distribution strategy does not affect simulation time for biologically realistic networks in CoreNEURON
Application of k-cut graph partitioning algorithm to address non-realistic network distribution cases
Demonstration of 25,000-cell simulation scaling capability with identification of GPU memory as the primary limiting factor

metrics.other: maximum network size: 25,000 cells; GPU memory as limiting factor; network latency impact decreases for larger networks

limitations: GPU memory capacity limits maximum network size to 25,000 cells; network latency impacts multi-site simulations of smaller networks.
primary_theme: distributed neuronal network simulation at scale
